---
title: "Matched conditions across a stimulus set"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Matched conditions across a stimulus set}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
library(mlvtoolbox)
```

Matching across a stimulus set can be feasible when each drawing is too small
to split. This minimal example has a corner in one drawing and a straight
contour in another, both ten pixels long.

```{r input}
drawings <- list(
  corner = mlv_drawing(list(rbind(c(5,5,10,5), c(10,5,10,10))),20,20),
  straight = mlv_drawing(list(matrix(c(5,5,15,5),1)),20,20))
spec <- feature_spec(c("length","orientation","curvature"), bins=2,
                     normalize=FALSE, estimator="arclength", curvature_scale=.5)
result <- design_subsets(drawings,spec,length_bounds=c(10,10),
  count_bounds=c(1,1),nuisance=c(length=0,orientation=10))
result
as.data.frame(result)
result$diagnostics$groups
result$diagnostics$per_drawing
```

The optimizer maximizes the difference in integrated absolute curvature at the
selected scale. Orientation matching uses raw length-weighted bin masses:
the tolerated L1 distance here is ten pixels. The resulting target difference
is 90 geometric degrees. This is a geometric construction, not evidence of a
perceptual effect. A and B are disjoint and contain only original whole contours.

```{r infeasible}
within_drawing <- design_subsets(drawings,spec,length_bounds=c(10,10),
  count_bounds=c(1,1),nuisance=c(length=0,orientation=10),mode="per_drawing")
within_drawing$status
```

Each source has only one contour, so it cannot provide two nonempty conditions.
The result reports proven infeasibility. A time or node limit has a different
meaning:

```{r time-limit}
limited <- design_subsets(drawings,spec,length_bounds=c(10,10),
  count_bounds=c(1,1),nuisance=c(length=0,orientation=10),time_limit=0)
limited$status
limited$solver[c("upper_bound","nodes","search_seconds")]
```

Zero time performs no search. `budget_exhausted` makes no feasibility claim.
If a limited run does find a solution, `feasible` retains its verified residuals
and a conservative objective bound. Only completed searches certify optimality
or infeasibility, within the declared numerical tolerance.

```{r persistence}
path <- tempfile(fileext=".rds")
saveRDS(result,path)
identical(readRDS(path)$selection,result$selection)
unlink(path)
```

The result preserves input geometry, provenance, source/contour IDs, specification
and reconstructed condition drawings. Physical measurements use visual degrees
with explicit input calibration. MAT/junction features can be requested as fresh
diagnostics after selection; they are not additive optimization constraints.
